title: Your Interval Either Contains It Or It Does Not
summary: Draw a population, then watch a hundred confidence intervals appear and roughly five of them miss. The ninety-five is a property of the recipe, not of the interval in front of you.

sources.title: Neyman, Outline of a Theory of Statistical Estimation Based on the Classical Theory of Probability (1937)
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, section 1.3.6.7.2: critical values of the t distribution
Morey, Hoekstra, Rouder, Lee and Wagenmakers, The Fallacy of Placing Confidence in Confidence Intervals (2016)
